name: Ecuadorian Hornado (Slow Roasted Pork) Bowls
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Slow-roasted achiote-garlic pork shoulder, served with rice and potatoes. Confidence note: source lists 10 servings but no nutrition panel, so est_cal is my estimate. Ecuadorian cuisine is completely absent from the catalog and achiote-paste is board-tracked, so the flavor base is already priced. | HARVEST: No nutrition panel published.
OVERRIDE Pork Shoulder: 8-10 lb BONE-IN skin-on shoulder (party roast, source serves 10); ~70% meat yield of 9 lb = 2860 g (protein clamp then portions to house norm)
intro_html: Walk through a market in Ecuador and you will find whole roasted pigs sitting on counters with a cook carving pieces off to order. That is hornado. The marinade is unapologetic about garlic, an amount that looks like a mistake until you taste it, plus achiote for color and lime for brightness. Roasted low for hours, the meat goes soft and the outside turns crackling. Served with potatoes, it is a plate worth the wait.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Lime Juice, 0.5 cups: ~$1.05. Buy 1 (covers about two batches).
Beef Broth, 4.25 cups: ~$1.35. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 32oz cartons.
Achiote Paste, 2.75 tbsp: ~$1.10. Buy 1 (covers about two batches).
Pantry seasonings (ground cumin, salt, black pepper): ~$0.67. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $36.44 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.60 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $40.86 across 14 servings, roughly $2.92 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $15.50 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $56.36. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). This is a big pork shoulder and it accounts for nearly the entire cost, which is exactly right for a dish where the pork is the whole show.
shop_smart: Buy the biggest bone-in pork shoulder you can fit in the pan. Price per pound drops as the roast gets bigger, and the bone is free flavor for the drippings.
Buy garlic in the mesh bag, not by the single head. This marinade uses a serious amount of it, and the bag price per head is a fraction of the loose price.
Achiote paste is a small block that lasts. One brick colors and seasons this roast and several others. It lives in the Hispanic aisle for a few dollars.
Save the drippings. The pan juices under a roast like this are the best sauce you will make all week, and you already paid for them. Skim the fat and spoon them over the potatoes.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mash the peeled garlic with salt into a paste, then blend it with the achiote paste, the lime juice, ground cumin and black pepper into a thick marinade.
Score the fat cap on the pork shoulder in a crosshatch and rub the marinade into every cut and across the whole roast. Cover and refrigerate overnight if you can.
Set the pork in a roasting pan, pour the beef broth into the bottom, dot the top with the butter, and cover tightly with foil.
Roast at 300F for about 4 hours, basting with the pan juices once an hour, until the meat pulls away from the bone.
Uncover, raise the oven to 425F, and roast 25 to 30 minutes more until the outside is deeply browned and crisp.
Boil the potatoes until tender while the roast rests, then pull the pork apart and spoon the skimmed pan juices over everything.
portion_html: Divide the potatoes across your 14 containers, then set your mixing pot of pulled pork on the scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and lay that exact weight alongside. Spoon the pan juices over the top. Every plate lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

head.description: Pork shoulder marinated in garlic, achiote and lime, then slow roasted until crisp and served with potatoes. A 14 serving Ecuadorian hornado for meal prep.
head.keywords: ecuadorian hornado, slow roasted pork shoulder, achiote pork, garlic pork roast, budget meal prep, cheap dinner ideas
steps: Blend the garlic, achiote paste, lime juice and cumin into a thick marinade.
Score the pork shoulder, rub the marinade in everywhere, and refrigerate overnight.
Roast covered at 300F with beef broth and butter for about 4 hours, basting hourly.
Uncover and roast at 425F for 25 to 30 minutes to crisp the outside.
Boil the potatoes, pull the pork, and spoon the skimmed pan juices over both.
